text:
ashley: quick follow-up from the observability RFC review — we need to lock down how cost attribution ties to traces/spans. high-level Q: do we attach billing metadata at span creation, or derive it in the pipeline?

kumar: attaching at span creation is ideal (low join complexity) but increases cardinality. worry about prometheus/metrics explosion if we ship as labels. :thinking:

maria: agree on tradeoff. we should keep span/resource attributes for detailed attribution and emit summarized metrics with bounded label sets for dashboards. i.e., full tags in tracing backend, reduced labels in metrics.

leo: proposed minimal attribution attributes: `service`, `model_variant`, `quantization`, `batch_size_group`, `route_id`, `customer_tier`. everything else stays in span-level baggage.

ashley: sounds good. also need to map GPU billing to requests. options: 1) per-span token counting and prorate GPU-seconds by token share, 2) sample traces and estimate distribution, 3) aggregate by batch and attribute evenly. thoughts?

kumar: 1) is most accurate but heavier (we'd instrument token_count in runtime). 2) cheap but noisy. 3) simplest but wrong for heterogenous sequences. leaning to 1) with sampling fallback for old clients.

maria: if we add `token_count` integer as span attribute, we can compute cost per token offline and backfill for missing traces. keep it out of prometheus labels.

leo: pipeline sketch: runtime -> otel spans (resource attributes incl. model_variant, quantization, hw_tier) -> kafka topic `spans-otel` -> processors (enrichment: attach gpu_hours from billing stream join) -> write to tracing backend + cost-store (parquet/day). metrics path: runtime -> metrics-emitter -> metric-aggregator -> prometheus/longterm store with reduced labels.

ashley: important: we must preserve request->batch mapping. add span link `batch_id`. this lets the batch-level aggregator attribute GPU time to constituent spans precisely.

kumar: examplesnippet for runtime span attrs: \n```\nresource.service.name=\"text-gen\"\nresource.attributes: model.variant=\"gptx-13b-q8\"\nspan.attributes: token_count=237, batch_id=\"b-2026-03-15-14-23-01\"\n```\n
maria: ops-bot ran quick cost estimate script on last week's prod: if we attribute by tokens, 90% of cost concentrated in 5% of requests (long context). we should consider a soft quota/alert for token outliers.

ops-bot: summary: job `cost-attrib-dryrun` finished, 7 failures (schema mismatch), sample output uploaded to s3://redwood-obsv/cost-dryrun/176789. Link: https://internal.s3/redwood-obsv/cost-dryrun/176789

leo: open questions: schema versioning approach, cardinality limits per metric, rollout plan for runtime instrumentation. propose: v1 spans with full attrs, v1 metrics with reduced labels; enable in canary region for 2 weeks, monitor telemetry volume.

ashley: action items:
- kumar: PR for runtime to add `token_count` + `batch_id` (due EOD Fri)
- leo: update pipeline diagram + add join logic with billing (due Mon)
- maria: alerts for token outliers + dashboard mockups (due next Wed)
- ops-bot: run another dry run after PR merge and report schema errors

kumar: noted, will open PR and ping here when ready.

maria: +1, will draft dashboards and share link.

ashley: thanks everyone. if anyone sees big perf/regressions from token_count attr, flag immediately and we can switch to sampling. :thumbsup:
